task: Write one sentence of your own using the word reprehensible. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know reprehensible should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Charging survivors for their lifeboat seats was reprehensible even by the shipping line's standards.
Improper conduct breaks the rules of the occasion — a ringing phone in the funeral row; reprehensible conduct breaks trust itself.
Monstrous goes past reprehensible: the reprehensible scheme deserves every word of blame it gets, while the monstrous one shocks the conscience so badly the words feel too small.

Disgraceful conduct brings public shame down on someone — the team, the family, the whole office winces in the open. Reprehensible aims at a different target: the deed itself deserves blame, whether or not anyone is watching or embarrassed. Disgrace needs an audience; reprehensible needs only the wrong.

Shameful conduct is dishonorable, and the accent is on the blush — the hot embarrassment the deed ought to raise. Reprehensible keeps the accent on the judgment: the conduct deserves open condemnation, blush or no blush. A shameful act makes people look away; a reprehensible one makes them speak up.

Reprehensible is the exact word because it doesn't just register wrongdoing — it demands open blame.
Regrettable conduct earns a wince; improper conduct breaks a rule.
Reprehensible conduct is the kind decent people feel obliged to stand up and name, which is what the word's own Latin machinery does: it reaches back and seizes the wrongdoer.

It describes the deed; its unit-mates denounce and decry describe what people then do about it.
